title: The effects of short versus long inter-set rest intervals in resistance training on measures of muscle hypertrophy: A systematic review
population: 6 trials in participants without known chronic disease or injury, training at least twice a week for at least four weeks.
key_findings: Compared short (60 seconds or less) with long (over 60 seconds) rests where rest was the only difference between groups.
Both short and long rests can produce hypertrophy.
Newer studies in trained people with more sensitive measures hint at an advantage for longer rests, but the authors call the evidence insufficient for a clear distinction.
methods: Systematic review of five databases without a pooled meta-analysis.
limitations: Only six studies with dissimilar designs; no quantitative synthesis.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
